In panel 3 the ribosome sits directly on the open channel, its polypeptide runs through the channel into the lumen with the signal sequence at the far end, and the SRP is by itself in the cytosol. In panel 4 a folded polypeptide lies free in the lumen, a short signal-sequence piece lies by itself near the closed channel, and the ribosome's two subunits lie apart from each other and from the parietal_cell_pump.title: The H⁺/K⁺ pump in a stomach parietal cell
parietal_cell_pump.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 252" role="img" aria-label="A parietal cell drawn as a rounded rectangle, its interior labelled parietal cell cytoplasm, pH ≈ 7. Its top membrane faces the stomach contents, labelled pH ≈ 1, and its bottom membrane faces the blood side. In the top membrane sits the H⁺/K⁺ pump. One arrow carries H⁺ from the cytoplasm up through the pump into the stomach contents; a second arrow carries K⁺ from the stomach contents down through the pump into the cell. Beside the pump's cytoplasmic face is written ATP → ADP + Pi."><defs><marker id="parietal_cell_pump_h" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="var(--review)"/></marker><marker id="parietal_cell_pump_k" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="var(--bridge)"/></marker></defs><text x="20" y="26" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">stomach contents</text><text x="20" y="45" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">pH ≈ 1</text><rect x="20" y="86" width="420" height="122" rx="18" fill="var(--mod2)" fill-opacity="0.04" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="205" y="56" width="54" height="60" rx="13" fill="var(--surface)"/><rect x="205" y="56" width="54" height="60" rx="13" fill="var(--accent)" fill-opacity="0.25" stroke="var(--accent)" stroke-width="1.6"/><line x1="222" y1="150" x2="222" y2="16" stroke="var(--review)" stroke-width="2.2" marker-end="url(#parietal_cell_pump_h)"/><line x1="242" y1="16" x2="242" y2="150" stroke="var(--bridge)" stroke-width="2.2" marker-end="url(#parietal_cell_pump_k)"/><text x="213" y="30" text-anchor="end" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="var(--review)">H⁺</text><text x="251" y="30" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="var(--bridge)">K⁺</text><text x="272" y="70" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">H⁺/K⁺ pump</text><text x="196" y="108" text-anchor="end" font-size="10.5" font-weight="700" fill="var(--accent)">ATP → ADP + Pi</text><text x="40" y="172" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">parietal cell cytoplasm</text><text x="40" y="191" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">pH ≈ 7</text><text x="20" y="236" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">blood side</text></svg>

macrophage_phagocytosis.title: Phagocytosis in a macrophage, step by step
macrophage_phagocytosis.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 640 214" role="img" aria-label="Four numbered panels, 1 to 4, joined by small arrows, each a slice of a macrophage with its plasma membrane along the top, the outside above and the macrophage cytoplasm below. 1: a rod-shaped bacterium touches receptor stubs on the macrophage membrane, and the membrane on either side has begun to extend up around it. 2: the membrane has wrapped all the way around the bacterium, which now sits in a pocket whose narrow neck is pinching off from the surface. 3: inside the cell, the rod sits in a membrane-bound
